item.title: Transposed Poisson structures in graded and algebroid geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.22629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We ask whether the transposed Leibniz rule $2z\cdot[x,y]=[z\cdot x,y]+[x,z\cdot y]$ survives the two passages that turn Poisson algebras into geometry, the shift of degree which produces Gerstenhaber algebras and the passage from algebras to algebroids. We introduce graded transposed Poisson algebras with a bracket of arbitrary degree and show that the parity of the degree decides which shape the answer takes. In even degree, over a unital base, such brackets are in bijection with homogeneous derivations, and on the exterior algebra of a vector bundle in degree zero they are exactly the gauge derivations of the bundle. In odd degree the bracket is forced to be the product with a single element of that degree, so a non-negatively graded algebra carries no non-zero transposed Gerstenhaber bracket. In particular, for a Lie--Rinehart algebra $(A,L)$, the Schouten--Rinehart Gerstenhaber algebra $\Lambda_A L$ is transposed if and only if the anchor and the bracket of $L$ both vanish. We then introduce transposed $F$-algebroids and classify those with an identity: if the rank is at least two the anchor vanishes and the structure is the datum of a derivation of the multiplication, while if the rank is one the bundle is trivialised by the identity and the structure is, globally, the Jacobi bracket of a single vector field. For the tangent $F$-algebroid of an $F$-manifold $M$ this forces $\dim M=1$.
item.dc:creator: Gianmarco La Rosa

item.title: An Adjoint Criterion for Left-Invariant $m$-Modified Conformal Vector Fields on Even-Dimensional Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.22759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a fixed positive real constant $m$, a real Lie algebra of even dimension $2k$ admits a nonzero left-invariant $m$-modified conformal vector field for some nondegenerate metric if and only if an adjoint operator has a nonzero real eigenvalue. In that case, a solution exists with neutral signature $(k,k)$ and zero conformal factor. As an application, we classify the admissible four-dimensional Lie algebras and metric signatures; the only Lorentzian exceptions among the admissible algebras are $\mathfrak{aff}(\mathbb{C})$ and the diamond algebra. On a pseudo-Riemannian manifold of arbitrary indefinite signature, a nonzero $m$-modified conformal vector field forces lightlike geodesic incompleteness, even when its conformal factor is variable.
item.dc:creator: Zhigang Li, Shaoqiang Deng, Hui Zhang

item.title: Type I estimates for the K\"ahler-Ricci flow II
item.description: arXiv:2610.22941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish geometric consequences of our Type I scalar curvature estimate for finite-time solutions of the K\"ahler-Ricci flow on compact K\"ahler manifolds. We prove a uniform global diameter bound and a Type I diameter bound for every fibre of finite time holomorphic contraction. These estimates yield Gromov-Hausdorff convergence to a unique compact metric space homeomorphic to the normal K\"ahler space determined by the limiting cohomology class. We also establish a local partial $C^0$ estimate for the normalized flow and show that the tangent shrinkers are normal complex analytic varieties with log terminal singularities.
item.dc:creator: Wangjian Jian, Jian Song

item.title: Ricci pinching on complete K\"ahler manifolds with nonnegative bisectional curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.22969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a connected complete K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension at least two with nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature and uniformly pinched Ricci curvature is compact or flat. This removes the Euclidean volume growth assumption from the flatness theorem of Liu and Ni \cite{LiuNi} for uniform Ricci pinching. We first construct a Lipschitz plurisubharmonic function with finite total Monge--Amp\`ere mass by solving a global Bellman equation. Weighted estimates for a holomorphic canonical section then give a finite top Ricci integral. Ricci pinching implies that the Ricci form belongs to $L^n$, and its Hodge heat evolution has zero top integral by a Stokes argument and scalar heat decay. \par\noindent\textit{Keywords.} K\"ahler manifolds, Ricci pinching, nonnegative bisectional curvature, Bellman equations, Monge--Amp\`ere mass.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhang Yin

item.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension one, two and three
item.description: arXiv:2610.23000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an exhaustive, self-contained, and coordinate-free structural classification of real Lie algebras of dimensions one, two, and three up to isomorphism. In dimensions one and two, the classification is governed entirely by the derived ideal and elementary derivation theory. In dimension three, we develop the classical exterior duality isomorphism $\Lambda^2\mathfrak{g} \cong \mathfrak{g}^* \otimes \Lambda^3\mathfrak{g}$ pioneered by Bryant and Milnor, which reduces the quadratic Jacobi identity on the $3 \times 3$ structure matrix $C = S + \hat{a}$ to the linear orthogonality relation $S \cdot a = 0$, where $a = \frac{1}{2}\chi$ is the trace covector. We systematically bifurcate the three-dimensional category into unimodular ($a = 0$) and non-unimodular ($a \neq 0$) sectors, completely recovering the nine classical Bianchi isomorphism classes (Bianchi types I through IX) alongside their continuous moduli invariants. Furthermore, we establish the Levi--Malcev decomposition for low dimensions, compute the exact minimal representation dimension $\mu(\mathfrak{g})$ via Ado's Theorem by constructing explicit matrix realizations in $\mathfrak{gl}(\mu, \mathbb{R})$, and formulate a deterministic, coordinate-free decision algorithm for algebra identification.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Nadjafikhah

item.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension four
item.description: arXiv:2610.23008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an exhaustive, coordinate-free, and self-contained classification of four-dimensional real Lie algebras up to isomorphism. In dimension three, classification schemes frequently exploit Bryant's classical exterior duality isomorphism $\Lambda^2\mathfrak{g} \cong \mathfrak{g}^* \otimes \Lambda^3\mathfrak{g}$, which reduces the Jacobi identity to an elegant linear algebraic condition on a single $3\times 3$ matrix. We explicitly demonstrate that this accidental isomorphism breaks down in dimension four due to the dimensional mismatch $\dim \Lambda^2\mathfrak{g} = 6 \neq 4 = \dim(\mathfrak{g}^* \otimes \Lambda^4\mathfrak{g})$, transforming the Jacobi identity into a non-linear system of 16 quadratic constraints on 24 structure constants. To overcome this geometric obstruction without relying on brute-force polynomial elimination, we employ an intrinsic Lie-theoretic reduction: the Levi--Malcev decomposition isolates the non-solvable sector into direct products with three-dimensional simple ideals, while the solvable sector is classified by anchoring the structure to its nilradical $\mathfrak{n}$, which is an intrinsic characteristic ideal. For codimension-one nilradicals ($\dim\mathfrak{n} = 3$), the problem is reduced to classifying outer derivations of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the Heisenberg algebra $\mathfrak{h}_3$ under the action of the automorphism group modulo global rescaling and central translations. For two-dimensional nilradicals, the structure is resolved via maximal abelian sub-algebras of $\mathfrak{gl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ lacking nilpotent elements. Complete proofs are supplied for all reductions, precise moduli parameter ranges are established to eliminate redundancies, and an explicit isomorphism dictionary is provided bridging our structural models with classical tabulations in mathematical physics.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Nadjafikhah

item.title: Spectral Schwarz Lemmas and Parallel Obstructions to Metric Comparison
item.description: arXiv:2610.23011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we characterize when comparison of contracted Chern curvatures implies comparison of Hermitian bundle metrics with the same constant on compact Hermitian bases. If the curvature contraction of the reference metric is semipositive, this implication holds for every Hermitian metric if and only if the kernel of this contraction contains no nonzero subbundle parallel with respect to the Chern connection of the reference metric. The equality terms of a $C^2$ spectral truncation identify the parallel summand on which comparison can fail, without regularity assumptions on the curvature kernel. We also establish a sharp operator estimate, with a constant independent of the bundle ranks, for holomorphic bundle maps on complete K\"ahler bases under curvature bounds and bounded base-map energy density. Smooth Schatten moments give global control without a separate boundedness assumption on the bundle map. Finally, we obtain rank bounds and conditions for vanishing on compact Hermitian bases from directional curvature traces over fiber subspaces. For higher-dimensional subspaces, these conditions allow mixed signs on individual fiber lines.
item.dc:creator: Xu Pang, Yao Sha, Ren Xin-An

item.title: Long-time existence of the Laplacian flow with Weyl tensor
item.description: arXiv:2610.23412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish integral extension criteria for the Laplacian flow of closed $G_2$-structures on compact $7$-dimensional manifolds $M$. Assuming a uniform lower bound for the scalar curvature, we prove that a finite-time solution extends smoothly whenever the spatial $L^p$ norm of the $77$-dimensional Weyl component $W_{77}$ remains uniformly bounded for some $p\ge 7/2$. We also obtain a mixed space--time extension criterion under the condition \[ W_{77}\in L^q(0,T;L^p(M,g(t))), \qquad \frac{7}{2}<p<\infty,\quad 1\le q<\infty,\quad \frac{1}{q}+\frac{7}{p}\le 2. \] In particular, finite space-time $L^4$ integrability of $W_{77}$ is sufficient for extension.
item.dc:creator: Chuanhuan Li, Yi Li, Kai Zheng

item.title: Entropy estimates and volume rigidity for graphs with positive Bakry-\'Emery curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.23417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a volume bound for weighted graphs with positive Bakry--\'Emery curvature through entropy estimates for the heat flow and characterize the equality case. As a consequence, if a connected unweighted graph $G=(V,E)$ satisfies the Bakry--\'Emery curvature--dimension condition $CD(2,\infty)$ with respect to the unnormalized Laplacian, then $$ |V|\le 2^d, $$ where $d$ denotes the maximum degree. Equality holds if and only if $G$ is a hypercube. We also establish an analogous volume rigidity result for the normalized Laplacian.
item.dc:creator: Yanlong Ding, Shiping Liu, Chiyu Zhou

item.title: Complete harmonic metrics and subharmonic functions on the complex plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.23441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper continues our previous work \cite{Miy6} on an extension of the Li--Mochizuki theorem concerning the existence and uniqueness of complete diagonal harmonic metrics on cyclic Higgs bundles over open Riemann surfaces. We consider the extended Hitchin equation associated with general subharmonic weight functions on the canonical bundle, not necessarily induced by holomorphic $r$-differentials. We establish uniqueness of complete solutions with determinant $1$ for arbitrary subharmonic weight functions, without additional regularity assumptions on them. We also prove that, on the complex plane, such a complete solution exists whenever the weight function is not identically $-\infty$. Furthermore, if $(\varphi_\epsilon)_{\epsilon>0}$ is a family of smooth subharmonic weight functions decreasing to such a weight function $\varphi$ as $\epsilon\searrow0$, the associated family of smooth complete solutions $(h_\epsilon)_{\epsilon>0}$ with $\det(h_\epsilon)=1$ converges monotonically to the unique complete solution $h$ associated with $\varphi$ and satisfying $\det(h)=1$.
item.dc:creator: Natsuo Miyatake

item.title: On flat metric nilpotent Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.23481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study flat left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics on nilpotent Lie groups. Associated with a flat metric Lie algebra $(\mathfrak{g},\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ there is a canonical affine action of the corresponding group on the vector space $\mathfrak{g}$, whose linear part is the Levi-Civita representation $L$. Combining this action with Scheuneman's theorem on pure translations in nilpotent affine groups, we prove that a flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra has a nontrivial kernel of $L$, that is, $\ker L\neq 0$. As a consequence, every $n$-dimensional flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra is a double extension of an $(n-2)$-dimensional flat metric nilpotent Lie algebra.
item.dc:creator: Huihui An, Zaili Yan, Hui Zhang, Shaoxiang Zhang

item.title: Closed geodesics on compact semi-Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the existence of closed geodesics on compact quotients of Lie groups endowed with left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics. We construct a compact, geodesically complete pseudo-Riemannian manifold that admits no closed geodesics. We also establish the existence of closed geodesics in several settings, with particular focus on the Lorentzian case.
item.dc:creator: Souheib Allout, Salah Chaib

item.title: Height of minimal surfaces: sharp thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The confinement theorem of [CM1] gives Euclidean volume growth for a proper minimal submanifold whose height over a plane is sublinear. Such volume growth places strong restrictions on the geometry. This leaves linear height as the natural borderline and raises the question of which, if any, linearly growing cones still force Euclidean growth. Here we determine this borderline sharply for proper holomorphic curves in $C^2$. There are two sharp thresholds for the aperture depending on the K\"ahler angle $\theta$ of the two-plane $\Pi$: $\tan(\theta/2)$ and $\cot(\theta/2)$. No proper holomorphic curve exists below the first, every such curve is algebraic below the second, and superquadratic proper holomorphic disks exist above the second. These conclusions extend to holomorphic submanifolds of arbitrary dimension and codimension. For stationary integral varifolds there are again three regimes: sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, narrow cones of aperture $\varepsilon$ force polynomial growth with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and wide cones allow arbitrarily fast growth. The order $\varepsilon^2$ is sharp: already in $R^3$, for every small $\varepsilon>0$ there are examples in a cone of aperture $\varepsilon$ whose volume grows at least like $r^{2+\frac45\varepsilon^2}$.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Holck Colding, William P. Minicozzi II

item.title: Three-circle inequalities for almost harmonic functions on cylinders
item.description: arXiv:2610.23648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The three-circle method was introduced into the blow-up analysis of harmonic maps by Qing and Tian [Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 1997]. We extend this method to a class of $(\tau,\epsilon)$-almost harmonic functions on long cylinders and establish three-circle inequalities for their weighted energies. These inequalities yield a dichotomy between exponential energy decay and asymptotic dominance of a critical Fourier mode, together with a characterization of the corresponding normalized limiting profiles. In the unweighted case, we prove convergence of the averaged neck curves and identify their limiting equations under additional structural assumptions. Applications include neck analysis and energy identities for harmonic maps, solutions of Rivi\`ere's equation, $\alpha$-harmonic maps, biharmonic approximations of harmonic maps, and Willmore surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Yuxiang Li, Wenjuan Qi

item.title: Solvability of complex Hessian equations corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.22524v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On compact Hermitian manifolds, we establish a framework using radial normalization for the solvability of complex Hessian equation in form type, corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials whose coefficients may not be constant functions. The solvability of a radial normalized equation is characterized by the existence of a C-subsolution at radial slope, which extends the results of Guo-Song to this setting.
item.dc:creator: Junbang Liu, Yulun Xu

item.title: Computing Fr\'echet on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.22592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Empirical averages are fundamental statistical primitives. On nonlinear spaces, their generalization, the Fr\'echet mean, generally lacks a closed-form solution, and its computation requires solving an optimization problem. We study the computation of intrinsic Fr\'echet means for data supported on an unknown compact $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M_{1}$ embedded in an ambient metric space $(X,d_{\operatorname{obs}})$. Such settings arise when observations are better represented in non-Euclidean spaces, like probability distributions in Wasserstein space. We assume access only to a local sampler on $M_{1}$ and the observation metric $d_{\operatorname{obs}}$, without knowledge of its intrinsic geometry. We propose a graph-based iterative algorithm that adaptively samples the manifold and approximates geodesic interpolation. Under mild assumptions, we establish an $O(1/T)$ expected objective gap guarantee using at most $\widetilde{O}(T^{4d+3})$ sampled points. As a byproduct of our analysis we extend the metric equivalence guarantees of ISOMAP from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces, which may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for computing intrinsic averages on unknown data manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Ian McPherson, Mauro Maggioni

item.title: Cross-ratios and first order ordinary differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22712v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the usefulness of the cross-ratio in the study of first order odes of the form $y^\prime=P_ny^n+P_{n-1}y^{n-1}+\ldots+P_1y+P_0,\;\; (P_i)_{0\leqslant i\leqslant n}\in K,\;n\geqslant1$, where $K$ is a differential field of characteristic zero with algebraically closed field of constants. We discover along the way many differential algebraic identity between solutions to that equation. We also explain why the cross-ratio of any four solutions to such an equation is in general not constant when $n\geq3$ by exhibiting an obstruction which prevents its constancy when $n\geq3$. Finally to any separable polynomial $P_\varphi(z)=z^{n+1}+\varphi_1z^n+\varphi_2z^{n-1}+\ldots+\varphi_{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, over a differential field of meromorphic function on some domain of $\mathbb C$ with the usual derivation we associate a uniquely defined first order ode of the form $y^\prime=P_ny^n+P_{n-1}y^{n-1}+\ldots+P_1y+P_0,\;\; (P_i)_{0\leqslant i\leqslant n}\in K$ such that every root of $P_\varphi(z)$ is a solution to the said differential equation.
item.dc:creator: Oumar Wone

item.title: Sharp improved Sobolev inequalities on $\mathbb{S}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.23069v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove sharp improved Sobolev inequalities on $\mathbb{S}^n$, $n\ge 4$, for functions whose critical density $|u|^{2n/(n-2)}$ has zero barycenter, without any symmetry assumption. The Dirichlet coefficient improves by the optimal factor $2^{-2/n}$, while the coefficient of the $L^2$ term remains one. Equality holds precisely for constant functions. This establishes the sharp form of Aubin's improved Sobolev inequality in every dimension $n\ge4$.
item.dc:creator: Juncheng Wei, Zetian Yan, Zikai Ye

item.title: mixed Hodge structures on the strictly upper triangular Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.23505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that, for $k\geq 3$, a lattice in the unitriangular Lie group $U_k(\mathbb{R})$ is the fundamental group of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety if and only if $k=3$. The proof uses the conjugation symmetry and weight conditions of mixed Hodge structure on the Malcev Lie algebra proven by Morgan. This result identifies a family of groups that must be excluded in the search for smooth quasi-projective varieties with torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of high nilpotency class.
item.dc:creator: Taito Shimoji

item.title: Arithmeticity, superrigidity, and totally geodesic submanifolds of infinite-volume hyperbolic manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23594v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given an infinite-volume convex cocompact hyperbolic manifold with Fuchsian ends and infinitely many maximal properly immersed totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two intersecting its convex core, we show that it (infinitely) covers an arithmetic hyperbolic manifold. This answers the general version of a question of Oh. As a byproduct of our techniques, we also give a Ratner-type classification of $\mathrm{SO}_0(m,1)$-invariant Radon measures whose support intersects the frame bundle of the interior of the convex core.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Miller

item.title: Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential
item.description: arXiv:2610.23752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion. At all other angles, the spectral network is dense in the surface and contains no finite webs, as expected. Physically, this example corresponds to a fundamental building block for a large class of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ QFTs with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$.
item.dc:creator: Omar Kidwai, Guillaume Tahar

item.title: Symplectic Lie groups and nilmanifolds associated with acyclic quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.23794v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give combinatorial criteria for the existence of left-invariant symplectic forms on the positive and full path Lie groups of finite acyclic quivers. For the nilpotent positive path Lie groups, the criterion also determines whether their compact quotients admit symplectic forms and forces the nilpotency step to be at most three. For the completely solvable full path Lie groups, we give a direct combinatorial criterion and an equivalent recursive criterion. In the symplectic case, the recursive procedure is realized by successive Hamiltonian reductions ending at an abelian symplectic Lie group. We characterize the existence of Lagrangian normal subgroups for a given form in both families, with applications to Lagrangian torus fibrations of compact nilmanifolds. We also describe the cohomology rings of the compact symplectic nilmanifolds and determine all Lefschetz ranks.
item.dc:creator: Yihao Zheng

item.title: A duality principle for the neighbourhood of manifolds and applications to counting rational points near curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.23797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish a duality principle relating the count of rationals near a manifold to a sparse counting problem for the dual. As applications, we give a short, self-contained proof of sharp bounds for planar curves under minimal regularity conditions and similarly, sharp upper bounds for non- degenerate space curves, again under minimal curvature conditions. This work recovers and extends the works of Beresnevich, Dickinson and Velani and of Vaughan and Velani on planar curves and independently proves and extends the results of Chen, Seeger, Srivastava and Technau on space curves, while providing a structural picture well-suited for generalisations. The re- sults and methods of this work precede the emergence of highly capable AI models.
item.dc:creator: Lauritz Streck

item.title: Uniform restriction lower bounds and nongeodesic common nodal curves in integrable systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.23836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a family of real analytic metrics on the two-torus, for which a fixed embedded nongeodesic circle is a nodal component of infinitely many real Laplace eigenfunctions. The examples address a question asked by Bourgain-Rudnick \cite{BR11}, and give a negative answer to the question asked by Toth-Zelditch \cite{TZ21} and Han \cite{Han}: whether a curve shared by infinitely many nodal sets must be geodesic. To explain the restriction obstruction, we prove uniform $L^2$ lower bounds for joint eigenfunctions of quantum completely integrable (QCI) systems under transverse crossing and isolation of a tangential characteristic branch, then extend to multi-branch setting. The results are used to characterize the possible joint nodal curves in the Liouville tori, narrowing down the choices. Finally, the counterexample realizes one possibility for which cancellation happens exactly on a nongeodesic curve.
item.dc:creator: Xianchao Wu, Xiao Xiao

item.title: Geometric Viewpoint of $L^\infty$ Estimates for Linearized Monge-Amp\`ere Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23848v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a Harnack inequality on Monge--Amp\`ere gradient graphs under suitable geometric bounds, giving us interior $L^\infty$ estimates for the linearized Monge--Amp\`ere equation. The proof combines Moser iteration on extrensic balls with a gradient estimate for the extrinsic distance function. The argument avoids the Caffarelli--Guti\'errez Harnack inequality and the engulfing and covering properties of Monge--Amp\`ere sections.
item.dc:creator: Arghya Rakshit, Derek Wu

item.title: Shannon entropy for harmonic metrics on cyclic Higgs bundles
item.description: arXiv:2410.08571v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface, $K_X$ its canonical bundle, and $T_X=K_X^{-1}$. A diagonal harmonic metric $h=(h_1,\dots,h_r)$ on a cyclic Higgs bundle of rank $r\geq 2$ associated with a holomorphic $r$-differential $q$ induces Hermitian metrics $H_j=h_j^{-1}\otimes h_{j+1}$ on $T_X$ for $j=1,\dots,r-1$, together with a possibly degenerate metric $H_r$ determined by $h_1,h_r$, and $q$. This construction depends on $q$ only through the subharmonic weight $\phi_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X$. In previous work, we extended harmonic metrics to solutions associated with arbitrary subharmonic weight functions $\varphi$, yielding analogous metrics $H_1,\dots,H_r$. For each nonzero real parameter $\beta$, we introduce a function on $X$, which we call entropy, that quantifies their mutual misalignment. By extending estimates of Dai--Li and Li--Mochizuki to general subharmonic weight functions, we obtain upper and lower bounds for $\beta>0$ when $H_1,\dots,H_{r-1}$ are complete and the weight is neither induced by a complete flat K\"ahler metric nor identically $-\infty$. The upper bound is $\log r$, the constant entropy associated with a complete flat K\"ahler metric, for which $H_1=\cdots=H_r$. The lower bound is the constant entropy associated with the weight $\varphi\equiv-\infty$. Furthermore, for every nonzero real $\beta$, we determine the asymptotic behavior, as $r\to\infty$, of the difference between these two entropy values, showing that it converges to a finite real number if and only if $\beta>-1$.
item.dc:creator: Natsuo Miyatake

item.title: Complete harmonic metrics and subharmonic functions on the unit disc
item.description: arXiv:2508.12848v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface with canonical bundle $K_X$ and holomorphic tangent bundle $T_X=K_X^{-1}$. For each integer $r\geq 2$, each $q\in H^0(K_X^r)$, and each choice of a square root of $K_X$, we obtain a cyclic Higgs bundle. A diagonal harmonic metric $h=(h_1,\ldots,h_r)$ induces Hermitian metrics $H_j=h_j^{-1}\otimes h_{j+1}$ on $T_X$ for $j=1,\ldots,r-1$, together with a possibly degenerate Hermitian metric $H_r$ determined by $h_1,h_r$, and $q$. We call $h$ complete if the K\"ahler metrics induced by $H_1,\ldots,H_{r-1}$ are all complete. Li--Mochizuki proved that if $q$ is nonzero unless $X$ is hyperbolic, there exists a unique complete harmonic metric on the corresponding cyclic Higgs bundle satisfying $\det(h)=1$. The Hitchin equation depends on $q$ only through the subharmonic weight $\phi_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X$. We establish uniqueness of complete solutions with determinant $1$ for general subharmonic weight functions $\varphi$ whose exponentials are $C^2$ outside a compact subset of $X$. On the unit disc $\mathbb D=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1\}$, we also prove that a real complete solution exists for every subharmonic weight function. We further establish a monotone approximation theorem. If $\varphi_\epsilon$ are smooth subharmonic weight functions on the discs $\mathbb D_\epsilon=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1-\epsilon\}$ decreasing to $\varphi$ as $\epsilon\searrow0$, the corresponding complete solutions $h_\epsilon$, normalized by $\det(h_\epsilon)=1$, converge monotonically to a complete solution $h$ associated with $\varphi$.
item.dc:creator: Natsuo Miyatake

item.title: On $q$-convex hypersurfaces in Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2604.20695v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that any closed, convex hypersurface in an $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-positive curvature operator is a rational homology sphere with finite fundamental group. The same conclusion holds for any $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-convex hypersurface, provided that the mean curvature satisfies a sharp pinching condition. Both results follow from more general vanishing and estimation theorems for the Betti numbers of closed $q$-convex immersed hypersurfaces in $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, under a lower bound on the average of the smallest $(n-p)$ eigenvalues of the curvature operator.
item.dc:creator: Giulio Colombo, Christos-Raent Onti

item.title: The Fried Conjecture for Morse-Smale Flows: A Survey on Ray-Singer and Milnor Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2607.16719v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper reviews the generalised Fried conjecture for Morse--Smale flows on compact Riemannian manifolds. We first establish the proper framework by constructing the twisted de Rham complex and deriving the Hodge decomposition, which underpins the definition of the Ray--Singer torsion. On the dynamical side, we characterise Morse--Smale vector fields, introducing the Ruelle Zeta function to encode the spectral data of closed orbits and {reviewing the Thom--Smale complex for purely gradient flows. In general, the local contributions of the critical elements of the flow are globally assembled via a Smale filtration to construct the Milnor metric} on the determinant line of the twisted cohomology. Finally, under the assumption of a unitary representation, we present the theorem proving the conjecture: the Ray--Singer metric coincides with the Milnor metric. Furthermore, we discuss the structure of the Milnor metric, which factors into the Ruelle Zeta function evaluated at zero and a specific contribution from the fixed points. We clarify that this object reduces to either the classical algebraic Thom--Smale torsion or the Ruelle Zeta function solely in the limiting cases of purely gradient or fixed-point-free flows.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Molinari

item.title: Complex Hyperbolic Immersions of Cheng--Yau Metrics on Thullen Domains
item.description: arXiv:2608.21911v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the homotheties of the complete Cheng--Yau K\"ahler--Einstein metrics on the two-dimensional Thullen domains $M(\mu)$, $\mu>0$, that admit K\"ahler immersions into $\mathbb{CH}^{\infty}$. With $\Ric(g_{\mathrm{CY}})=-3g_{\mathrm{CY}}$, an immersion of $c\,g_{\mathrm{CY}}$ exists exactly when $0<\mu\leq\mu_+$ and $0<c\leq3\min\{1,\mu\}/(\mu+2)$. The critical parameter $\mu_+>1$ is characterized by an explicit equation, and its endpoint is included. Every admissible metric has a proper global K\"ahler embedding. The same parameter interval classifies immersibility into flat and projective Hilbert space, where every positive homothety admits a proper global embedding. Beyond the wall, all three targets are excluded at every positive scale. The proof combines an algebraic normalization of the Cheng--Yau equation, all-order coefficient estimates, and complex continuation of a scalar flow. For $\mu\neq1$, the resulting complete nonhomogeneous examples disprove proposed K\"ahler--Einstein rigidity conjectures in the complex-hyperbolic and flat Hilbert settings. We also prove a complementary rigidity theorem for Bergman--Hartogs domains and construct complete $\eta$-Einstein Sasakian manifolds with nonhomogeneous Riemannian metrics and proper global Sasakian embeddings into the infinite-dimensional Heisenberg space form.
item.dc:creator: Mirel Caib\u{a}r, Andrea Loi

item.title: Conformally symplectic structures and the Lefschetz condition
item.description: arXiv:2403.12304v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This short note provides a symplectic analogue of Vaisman's theorem in complex geometry. Namely, for any compact symplectic manifold satisfying the hard Lefschetz condition in degree 1, every locally conformally symplectic structure is in fact globally conformally symplectic, whenever there is a mutually compatible almost complex structure.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Lejmi, Scott O. Wilson

item.title: On the torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of smooth quasi-projective varieties of rank up to seven
item.description: arXiv:2510.09026v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth quasi-projective variety. Assume that the (topological) fundamental group $\pi_1(X, x)$ is torsion-free nilpotent. We show that if the first Betti number $b_1(X) \le 3$, then $\pi_1(X, x)$ is isomorphic to either $\mathbb{Z}^n$ for $n = 1, 2, 3$, a lattice in the Heisenberg group $H_3(\mathbb{R})$ or $\mathbb{R} \times H_3(\mathbb{R})$. Moreover, we prove that $\pi_1(X, x)$ is abelian or $2$-step nilpotent if its rank is less than or equal to seven. More precisely, we determine the real nilpotent Lie groups in which torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups can be embedded as lattices for ranks up to six and seven, respectively. Our main results are a partial positive answer to a question on nilpotent (quasi-)K\"ahler groups posed by Aguilar and Campana.
item.dc:creator: Taito Shimoji

item.title: The capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski problem for $p>q$ in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.07158v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq3$, admits a unique positive smooth strictly convex solution for any prescribed positive smooth function $f$ when $p>q$ and the contact angle satisfies $\theta\in(0,\pi/2)$. Earlier results for $p>q$ either required the additional condition $q\leq1$ or were restricted to $n=2$. We reduce the problem to a Monge--Amp\`ere type equation with a Robin boundary condition on a spherical cap. By constructing a new auxiliary function for the global $C^2$ estimate, we overcome these limitations and completely resolve the case of $p>q$ in higher dimensions, i.e., prove existence and uniqueness throughout the case of $p>q$, without any further restriction on $p$ or $q$.
item.dc:creator: Ya Gao

item.title: Stability for a formally determined Lorentzian inverse problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.10413v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the inverse problem of recovering a potential $q$, depending on space and time, in the wave equation $(\Box_g+q)u=0$ on a Lorentzian manifold. We prove Lipschitz stability for a formally determined version of this problem under a \textit{null-cone foliation} assumption. As a consequence, we obtain uniqueness for the Lorentzian Calder\'on problem in a fixed conformal class. Our approach uses distorted spherical waves.
item.dc:creator: Spyridon Filippas, Lauri Oksanen

item.title: Localization of Lagrangian Floer homology for $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.14468v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith. The main construction is a stabilized chain complex. At every invariant intersection point we adjoin the Morse complex of a finite-dimensional normal spectral sphere, whose generators lie in free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbits. The differential counts holomorphic strips coupled to sphere half-trajectories by a one-sided weighted asymptotic evaluation. We prove transversality, a uniform spectral cutoff, and the compactification and gluing statements needed for the chain identity. The stabilized complex is quasi-isomorphic to the ordinary Floer complex and contains the complex of the fixed data as a subcomplex with free quotient, so the algebraic Smith inequality applies.
item.dc:creator: Erkao Bao, Tyler Lawson, Cheuk Yu Mak
